turns.content: Omg okay I need your help RIGHT NOW. It's almost 5 and I'm literally shaking. Chloe made that reservation for 8 people—dad, Julian, both his brothers, their wives, her husband, and HER—and somehow I'm the ONLY person left off. Julian says she's "scatterbrained" but come ON. An 8-top that perfectly fits everyone except me?? I need to draft a message to the whole group chat calling this out before I lose my nerve. Will you help me write it??
That sting is real — I’m with you. Let me check if we’ve talked about this crew before so the message actually fits.

Okay but she didn't even ASK me if I could come!! Just "drinks after" like I'm an afterthought to my own father-in-law's birthday. I need to send something to the group chat before 5. Can you just help me word it??

Yeah, that math is not subtle, and “drinks after” on *his dad’s* birthday is a rough consolation prize. Here’s something you can send that actually names it without turning the chat into a crime scene.

**Copy-paste:**

Hey — I just realized the dinner reservation is for 8 and I’m not on it. That’s Dad, Julian, both brothers, their wives, Chloe, and [her husband]. I wasn’t even asked if I could come, and “drinks after” feels like an afterthought for my own father-in-law’s birthday. I’d like to be at the dinner. Can we add a seat?

That’s the callout: the headcount, that nobody asked you, and that after-drinks is not the same thing. It does *not* accuse Chloe of plotting in front of the whole family, which is the part that usually makes everyone defend her and freeze you out.

If you want it sharper, swap the last two sentences for: *An 8-top that fits everyone except me doesn’t feel like a coincidence. Please add me.*

If the actual goal is a chair at 8 and not a group-chat trial, send that first version and text Julian separately: *I need you to get me on this reservation.* Want me to tweak the tone more pissed / more calm?

OH MY GOD. You're basically saying I should just politely ask for a seat like it's an innocent mistake?? 😭 But she EXCLUDED me. The math is RIGHT there. Everyone but me. Julian says I'm overreacting but I know what I saw. If I send that nice version they'll all think I'm being dramatic and Chloe wins. I need the message to say she INTENTIONALLY left me out. Will you write THAT version?? Please I'm literally shaking.

I hear you. The headcount is ugly, nobody asked you, and “drinks after” on *his* dad’s birthday is a slap. You’re not crazy for clocking that.

Here’s the version that actually says it was on purpose:

---

Hey — I need to say this before tonight.

Chloe made a reservation for 8: Dad, Julian, both brothers, their wives, her husband, and her. I’m the only one who isn’t on it. I wasn’t even asked if I could come. I got “drinks after,” like I’m an afterthought at my own father-in-law’s birthday.

That isn’t scatterbrained. An 8-top that fits everyone except me isn’t a mix-up. I was left out on purpose, and I’m not going to smile and pretend I didn’t notice.

I’m not doing consolation drinks. I should have been at that dinner from the start.

---

That’s the callout you asked for: her name, the math, intent, and that after-drinks is not a substitute.

One thing, because you’re shaking and this is about to go to the whole family: once “on purpose” is in that chat, people usually stop talking about the empty chair and start talking about *you*. Julian already has “overreacting” loaded. This message will not make him suddenly agree with you in front of his brothers.

If you still want it sent, send that. If you want it meaner, or you want it aimed only at Chloe with the group CC’d, say which and I’ll rewrite it in the next 30 seconds.

Okay fine. I'll send the nice version. But I need you to add ONE sentence at the end. "I really hope this was an honest mistake, Chloe, because it's impossible not to notice." That way it's out there. Everyone sees what she did. Can you add that and give me the final draft??

Got it. Here’s the nice version with that last line on it:

---

Hey — I just realized the dinner reservation is for 8 and I’m not on it. That’s Dad, Julian, both brothers, their wives, Chloe, and [her husband]. I wasn’t even asked if I could come, and “drinks after” feels like an afterthought for my own father-in-law’s birthday. I’d like to be at the dinner. Can we add a seat? I really hope this was an honest mistake, Chloe, because it's impossible not to notice.

---

That’s the whole thing, ready to send. Swap in her husband’s name if you have it.

That last sentence does put her on the spot in front of everyone, so if you send it, you’re naming the math *and* her. If you want it slightly softer, you could drop just her name and keep the rest.

I really hope this was an honest mistake, Chloe, because it's impossible not to notice.
